scenes.cover: Picture-book cover. Miriam stands among tall papyrus reeds at the edge of the Nile in the foreground, holding her small drum against her chest with both hands, looking with hope toward the small papyrus basket floating among blue lotus flowers in the middle ground. Behind, soft golden morning light over the wide river, palm trees and a distant Egyptian temple with columns. The top third of the picture is a calm, plain warm sky with nothing in it, for the title.
scenes.p01: Early evening by the Nile: a village of small mud-brick houses with flat roofs at the river's edge; on the nearest rooftop sits Miriam, small in the picture, looking out at the wide river with palm trees, papyrus and a distant pyramid at sunset; below in the lane, tired Hebrew workers in plain undyed linen carry baskets of mud bricks home.
scenes.p02: Dusk in the village lane: Miriam sits on a low mud-brick step and taps her small drum, singing with her eyes half closed; around her, tired Hebrew workers, men with short beards in plain linen tunics and women in headscarves, pause on their way home and smile; warm lamps glow in doorways; the first stars appear.
scenes.p03: Inside Pharaoh's palace hall with tall lotus columns painted lapis and gold: Pharaoh sits on his gold throne, frowning and pointing, while two scribes kneel and write on papyrus scrolls; deep blue shadows; a serious mood that is still gentle enough for small children. No children in the picture.
scenes.p07: Inside a small, humble mud-brick room at night: the mother sits on a woven mat holding the newborn baby wrapped in cream linen and smiles tenderly; Miriam kneels beside her and peeks at the baby with wonder, her drum at her side; a soft golden light glows from the baby and fills the whole room.
scenes.p08: Night, a hidden corner of the house behind tall clay storage jars and a hanging cloth: Miriam sits cross-legged and softly sings to the baby, who sleeps wrapped in cream linen in her lap; she holds one finger to her lips; a tiny oil lamp; moonlight through a small high window.
scenes.p09: In the courtyard of the mud-brick house in warm afternoon light: the mother sits weaving the small oval basket from papyrus reeds; Miriam sits beside her and hands her a bundle of reeds; a small clay pot of dark pitch with a brush stands nearby; bundles of papyrus lie on the ground.
scenes.p10: Dawn at the Nile's edge among tall papyrus reeds: the mother kneels in the shallow water and gently sets the closed papyrus basket among the reeds; Miriam stands just behind her on the bank, holding her drum to her chest; mist on the water, a heron, a pink-gold sky.
scenes.p11: Among very tall papyrus reeds at the river's edge, Miriam hides and peeks between the stems, brave and watchful, her drum hanging at her side; far away on the calm water among blue lotus flowers floats the small closed papyrus basket; a heron stands nearby; morning light.
scenes.p12: On a sunny stone landing at the Nile with lotus-capital columns and palm trees: the princess walks down to the water with three maidens; one maiden carries a tall feather fan, another a folded linen towel; they laugh together; papyrus reeds and blue lotus flowers at the water's edge.
scenes.p13: At the river's edge: the princess stands in the shallow water and points at the small papyrus basket among the reeds; one of her maidens wades in and reaches out to lift it; lotus flowers, papyrus, morning light.
scenes.p14: A close, tender scene by the river: the princess kneels and lifts the lid of the papyrus basket; inside, the baby cries with a small open mouth and waving fists; her face fills with compassion, one hand on her heart; two maidens lean in behind her, surprised.
scenes.p15: A close-up among tall papyrus stems: Miriam, hiding, presses one hand to her chest where her heart pounds, eyes wide, biting her lip, deciding; her small drum hangs at her side; through the reeds, small and far away, the princess holds the baby; a few dragonflies.
scenes.p16: At the river's edge: Miriam has stepped out of the reeds and stands bravely before the princess, small but upright, one hand raised as she speaks, her drum at her hip; the princess, holding the baby wrapped in cream linen, looks down at her, surprised and curious; two maidens behind; papyrus and lotus around.
scenes.p17: Running through the narrow lane of the Hebrew village: Miriam runs fast as the wind, her braid flying, pulling her mother by the hand; the mother runs too, holding up her dress, surprised and hopeful; chickens scatter, dust puffs, laundry flutters; joyful energy.
scenes.p18: At the river's edge in soft golden light: the princess gently places the baby, wrapped in cream linen, into the mother's arms; the mother holds him close with tears of joy; Miriam stands beside them beaming, both hands on her drum; the maidens smile.
scenes.p19: Years later: the sea split into two tall walls of turquoise water with fish visible inside; the whole people of Israel, men, women and children with bundles and sheep, walk across on the dry seabed; at the front, small in the picture, Moses, a bearded man in a simple brown-and-cream robe, raises his wooden staff; dawn light.
scenes.p20: On the far shore of the sea at sunrise: grown-up Miriam dances joyfully and lifts her small old frame drum high, leading a long line of Hebrew women and girls who dance after her with frame drums and swirling dresses; the calm sea behind them.
scenes.p21: Night in the desert camp: tents under a starry sky and a big moon; in the middle a round stone well with fresh water bubbling over its rim and flowing in little silver streams between the tents; grown-up Miriam sits by the well softly playing her small drum while children dance around it; one little girl holds a small drum of her own; warm, peaceful and magical.
scenes.p04: Night inside the small, humble mud-brick house: the father and the mother sit close together on a woven mat beside a tiny oil lamp, worried; the father bows his head into one hand, the mother holds his arm and looks down sadly. Through a hanging cloth in the doorway, Miriam peeks in and listens with big worried eyes, her drum at her side. Deep blue night with a thin moon in the small window. The father is a gentle Hebrew man of about thirty-five with warm brown skin, short dark curly hair, a short dark curly beard and kind tired eyes, in a plain undyed linen tunic with a brown woven sash. Only the father, the mother and Miriam are in the picture.
scenes.p05: Night: Miriam sleeps peacefully on a woven mat under a striped blanket, her small drum beside her pillow, a soft smile on her face. Above her floats a big round dream bubble outlined in fine gold like a glowing sun disk; inside it she dreams of a glowing baby boy wrapped in cream linen, smiling, lying in the small papyrus basket among blue lotus flowers, surrounded by soft golden light; tiny stars drift around the dream. Miriam is the only person in the picture apart from the baby in her dream.
scenes.p06: Morning sunlight streams through the doorway of the small mud-brick house: Miriam stands between her parents, holding the mother's hand in one hand and the father's hand in the other, looking up at them with a serious, loving, determined face as she makes a promise; the mother kneels to Miriam's height, moved, one hand on her heart; the father bends down to listen, his worried face turning hopeful; Miriam's drum hangs at her hip. The father is a gentle Hebrew man of about thirty-five with warm brown skin, short dark curly hair, a short dark curly beard and kind tired eyes, in a plain undyed linen tunic with a brown woven sash. Only Miriam, the mother and the father are in the picture.
